name: Spain: Other DOs
court: SPAIN - OTHER DOs *CERTIFIED SOMMELIER EXAM ONLY*

outcome.certified: After studying this section, a student will know the styles of wine made in selected DOs beyond the classic regions.

rows.certified: País Vasco: Atlantic coast of northern Spain; Murcia: Mediterranean coast of southeast Spain; DO Pago: Distributed throughout Spain, concentrated in Castilla-La Mancha
País Vasco: Moderate maritime (a.k.a. Green Spain); Murcia: Warm Mediterranean
Murcia: Historically, Monastrell vines were ungrafted due to the sandiness of the soil.
País Vasco: Modern: temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks; DO Pago: Primarily international styles of red wine.
País Vasco: Hondarrabi Beltza; Murcia: Monastrell (Mourvèdre); DO Pago: International grape varieties

País Vasco: Bizkaiko Txakolina DO; Primarily dry white. Reds and rosés (rosados) are rare. Wines are lightly effervescent with high acidity. Meant for early consumption.; Arabako Txakolina DO; Primarily dry white. Reds and rosés (rosados) are rare. Wines are lightly effervescent with high acidity. Meant for early consumption.; Getariako Txakolina DO; Primarily dry white. Reds and rosés (rosados) are rare. Wines are lightly effervescent with high acidity. Meant for early consumption.; Murcia: Jumilla DO; Dry red wine focused on pure Monastrell and Monastrell-based blends.; DO Pago: Understand the concept and definition of the DO Pago. **It is not necessary to memorize the list of Pago producers.

País Vasco: Primarily dry white wine. Reds and rosés (rosados) are rare. Wines are lightly effervescent with high acidity. Meant for early consumption.; Murcia: Dry red wine; DO Pago: Primarily red wine
DO Pago: Understand the place of DO Pago in Spanish wine hierarchy. **It is not important to learn any of their names at this level.

Murcia: Avoided phylloxera until 1980s.; DO Pago: Vinos de Pagos was first created in 2003. There are 20 Vinos de Pagos as of 2022, serving the purpose of producer appellations outside of traditional winemaking styles.
País Vasco: Txakoli whites are traditionally served with oily seafood.
